You are preparing a presentation fbr a science project on traditional medicine.
You
found some interesting information in the article below and are now making your
outline.
Ayurvedic Medicine
The idea of health and wellness relates to the state of feeling physically,
mentally, and socially healthy and the process needed to achieve this state.
Western medicine focuses mostly on physical health with evidence-based
approaches.
However, many so-called "traditional medicine'' practices focus on
more than just physical health
Traditional medicine is based on the beliefs and
cultural practices of a society.
It is often associated with religious or spiritual
beliefs and focuses on mental health alongside physical health
One type
of
traditional medicine
is Ayurvedic medicine.
It originated in lndia more than
5,000 years ago・The name comes froln the word Ayurveda, meaning the
science of life.
Ayurvedic medicine focuses on reducing the symptoms of and
increasing resistance to disease, reducing stress, and creating a life filled with
balance and harmonv.
‐
Ayurvedic medicine often uses herbs.
These herbs are used to treat a
varietv of svmptoms・Research on the effects of Avurvedic treatments
is
ご
limited! but some studies have shown them to have benefits.
Ashwagandha,
fbr example, is an Ayurvedic herb that has been shown to promote relaxation.
Garlic is used in Ayurvedic treatments to reduce cholesterol, which can cause
heart disease.
Other herbs can increase cognitive functions, in other words,
enhance mental
abilities, reduce joint pain, or even regulate hormones, which
are chemicals Droduced bv the bodv.
A benefit of using Ayurvedic medicine
is that many of the herbs used
can be grown at home・Plants such as lemongrass, ground ivy, aloe vera, and
Indian indigo can easily be grown at home.
These can be used to make teas,
oils, powders, and pastes to be taken as medicine.
Growing herbs at home can
ensure their quality when used as medicine.
It can also reduce the amount of
money spent on purchasing products made from these herbs.
－（2）－26－

As mentioned above, there
is limited research on the effectiveness of
Ayurvedic treatments.
However, there are some clinical trials that show
Ayurvedic medicine works・A 2013 study looked into pain relief among 440
participants
They were split into two groups: one group using Ayurvedic
medicine, and the other using Western medicine.
Seven patients
in the
Ayurvedic treatment group were removed from the study due to liver function
problems; however, the participants in both groups reported similar reductions
in pain.
Another study on chronic joint pain - pain that lasts three or more
months
found that compared to participants who used Methotrexate (MTX),
a drug widely used for this treatment, those who used Ayurvedic medicine
reported fewer negative effects.
The participants using Ayurvedic medicine
also experienced positive outcomes similar to those taking the drug.
While the outcomes of the research sound positive, people interested in
using Ayurvedic medicine need to understand the commitment that must be
made.
First and foremost is that no two people are the same, and as such, how
long it will take for a treatment to be effective can differ.
For some people,
three months may be
all that is needed for the effects to show, while others
may have to wait a year or more・Other Ayurvedic treatments may require
lifestyle changes to ensure the medicine is used at strict times, together with
the right food, as part of a specific diet.
There are
also potential risks with Ayurvedic medicine.
First, many
Ayurvedic medicines may contain metals or minerals that are known to be
dangerous to humans.
Additionally, certain herbs contained in these medicines
may in fact be toxic.
A survey found that 40% of participants using Ayurveda
medicine who were offered heavy metals screening had increased levels
of
lead and mercury in their blood.
Exposure to these substances can negatively
affect the human body.
While the concerns about Ayurvedic medicine are serious, there
is no
doubt that the treatments can be effective.
Western medicine is beginning to
find truth in some of the traditional beliefs these treatments come from.
As with
all medical treatments, patients should consult an expert before
beginning.
Always seek advice from a doctor or
a qualified professional.
Ayurvedic medicine
is worth further study as a potential alternative fOr those
who cannot obtain good results from western medicine for symptoms such as
pain or memory problems.
－②－27－
